title: CreateCVOnline — full-site test checklist
subtitle: Grounded in this codebase: 61 templates, 6 categories, 3 languages, PayPal, Firebase. Counts and route names below are read from the source, not guessed — if a number on screen disagrees with a number here, that is the finding.
principles: Measure the rendered artefact, not the source. Nearly every real defect in this project was invisible in the code and obvious in the built page: a footer that asked for the wrong locale, a search box advertising terms that returned nothing, a price computed from the wrong count. Open the page, read what it actually says.

Test the failure paths in all three languages. The half-English error card survived weeks of review because it only appeared when a payment failed — every screenshot of a working checkout looked perfectly translated.
NEXT_PUBLIC_* is inlined at build time. Changing one in the hosting dashboard does nothing until the next deploy. If you changed one, confirm the deploy happened after you saved it.
Use a fresh incognito window. A warm session and an existing locale cookie hide most auth, paywall and language bugs.
Keep the browser console open the whole time. Several bugs here logged loudly and showed nothing on screen.

sections.name: Before you start
sections.note: Five minutes here saves an afternoon of testing the wrong build.

items.t: The deployed commit is the one you pushed
items.d: Vercel → Deployments → top entry. Compare the SHA with `git log --oneline -1`. A green deploy of yesterday's commit looks identical to a fresh one.

items.t: The build finished without warnings you have not read
items.d: Open the build log. `next build` reports unused variables, failed prerenders and missing env vars, and nobody reads it until something breaks.

items.t: Two accounts ready: one free, one paid
items.d: Most quota and paywall bugs only appear on the free account. Grant the paid one through /admin so you are not spending sandbox money on every pass.

items.t: Fresh incognito window, console open, network tab open
items.d: Console for the errors, network for the request bodies — you will need both in the payment section.

items.t: A phone on the same page as the desktop
items.d: Not DevTools' device mode. Real touch targets, real font rendering, real keyboard.

sections.name: Marketing pages — English
sections.note: 28 public routes. For each: it renders, exactly one <h1>, no `undefined` or `NaN` anywhere on the page, header and footer present, no console errors.

items.d: Home. Hero, template preview strip, CTAs all resolve.

Free / Pro $9 per month / Lifetime $69. Check the FREE plan claims **20 templates, 18 of them rated 5/5 for ATS** — those two numbers are computed from the registry. If they read 16 and 5, the computation broke.
**61** templates, **6** categories (modern, corporate, creative, technology, classic, ats). Count them.
Each of the 6 filters narrows the grid and the count matches. Clearing returns to 61.
Search the exact terms the placeholder advertises. Every suggested term must return results — a placeholder promising a word that returns zero is worse than an empty box.

items.t: Phrase search returns the phrase, not the words
items.d: Search `two column`. It must return the templates that are two-column (17), not every template matching `two` OR `column` (20). This exact off-by-three is how the bug was found.
Preview image loads, description present, CTA works, related templates resolve.
Both landing variants.
Four keyword landing pages.
Three more.
ATS landing pages. Any template count quoted here must match the 18 figure.
Index plus at least three roles.
At least three professions.
Static content pages.
The form posts to /api/contact. Submit it and confirm the message arrives; a contact form that silently fails is the most expensive kind of broken.
Index paginates, at least three articles render, no broken images.
Legal pages. Every footer link resolves — these are the links nobody clicks until a customer does.

items.t: Every footer and nav link, clicked
items.d: Tedious, and it is where dead links live.

sections.name: French — /fr

items.d: Fully French. No English strings.
Pricing. Plan names, taglines, all 15 highlights, the billing cadence, and the currency.
Gallery. All 61 templates with French taglines.

items.t: The filter bar is in French

French description, and the URLs in the page point at /fr/ paths.

View source. Screen readers and Google both use it.
Canonical points at the /fr URL, not the English one. hreflang lists en, fr, de and x-default, and each points back.

items.t: JSON-LD uses French URLs and images
items.d: The structured data on the French gallery used English URLs and English preview images. View source and read the ld+json block.

sections.name: Language switching and the locale cookie
sections.note: The subtlest bugs in the project live here. All four items below were real.

items.t: The switcher changes the language and it sticks
items.d: EN → FR, then navigate to two more pages. Still French.

items.t: A French preference survives a visit to /dashboard
items.d: Switch to French, then open /dashboard, then go back to the marketing site. If you are in English, the cookie was reset — /dashboard is not in a translated cluster and only paths that are may write the cookie.

items.t: Prefetch does not change the language
items.d: Set French. Scroll a page with many in-viewport links so Next prefetches them. Then navigate. Still French. Prefetches used to rewrite the locale cookie, and curl never reproduced it — this one needs a real browser.

items.t: A signed-in profile locale beats the cookie
items.d: Set the account language to German in /dashboard/settings, then set the cookie to French by visiting /fr. Signed in, you should get German.

items.t: The preference survives sign-out and sign-in
items.d: Set French, sign out, sign in. Still French.

items.t: Switching language inside the editor does not lose work
items.d: Type into a CV, switch language, confirm nothing was dropped and your renamed sections kept their custom names.
New address. Account created, verification email arrives.

items.t: The unverified state is honest about what is blocked
items.d: Sign in before verifying. You should be told what to do, not silently limited.

items.t: The verification link works, and works only once
items.d: Click it. Then click it again.
Both a brand-new Google account and one that already has an email/password account with the same address.
Request → email → reset → sign in with the new password → old password rejected.

items.t: Wrong password and unknown email give useful, localised errors
items.d: In all three languages. Auth errors are an error path, which is exactly where English leaks.
DevTools → Application → Cookies. If JavaScript can read it, a single XSS becomes account takeover.

items.t: Protected routes bounce to /login and come back
items.d: Open /dashboard/cvs signed out. You should land on /login?next=… and be returned to /dashboard/cvs after signing in.

items.t: Sign out really ends the session
items.d: Sign out, then press Back. No dashboard content, no cached private data. Then reload.

items.t: An expired session mid-action is handled
items.d: Sign in, delete the session cookie in DevTools, then try to save a CV. You should be asked to sign in, not shown a stack trace.

items.t: /dashboard loads and the quota meters are right
items.d: On a free account: 0 of 2 CVs, 0 of 5 downloads.

items.t: Create, rename, duplicate, delete a CV
items.d: All four, and each survives a page reload.
List and detail.

items.t: The free CV limit is enforced by the SERVER
items.d: Create 2 CVs on a free account. The button should disappear — then POST to /api/cvs directly from the console and confirm the server also refuses. A limit enforced by hiding a button is not a limit.

items.t: The completeness score changes as you fill the CV
items.d: And is not stuck at a number.

items.t: /dashboard/account shows the right plan and expiry
items.d: Pro should show 31 days from purchase. Lifetime should show no expiry. Free should show no expiry either — not "expired".
And nothing belonging to anyone else.
Profile fields save; the language switcher works.
Premium templates marked locked on free, unlocked on Pro.

items.t: A brand-new account's empty dashboard reads well
items.d: Empty states are shipped once and reviewed never. Register a fresh account and look at it.

items.t: Split pane on desktop, three tabs on mobile
items.d: Both layouts, both usable.
Edit, wait, reload without touching a save button. The change is there.
Several steps deep, including after a template switch.
With a mouse and with touch.
Then switch language: a section YOU renamed must keep your name, while untouched ones translate.
Fill a CV completely, switch template three times, and confirm nothing was dropped — including custom sections.
Each visibly changes the preview and persists.

items.t: Paper size A4 and US Letter
items.d: Both, and the PDF matches the choice.
Known dependency: this needs Firebase Storage enabled on the project. If it fails, check that before debugging the code.

items.t: Page-break guides match the real PDF
items.d: Add content until a guide appears, export, and compare. A guide that lies is worse than no guide.

items.t: A CV long enough to be 2 pages, and one long enough to be 3+
items.d: Both in the preview and the PDF.

items.t: A completely empty CV does not crash the preview
items.d: New CV, type nothing, look at the preview.
300-character job title, emoji, accented and non-Latin characters, a URL with no spaces. Nothing should overflow the page or break the layout.

sections.name: Templates — 61 of them
sections.note: The automated suite covers all 61 against full, sparse and empty CVs. This is the human pass: does it look like something you would send to an employer.

items.t: One template from each of the 6 categories, with a FULL CV
items.d: modern, corporate, creative, technology, classic, ats.

items.t: The same six with a SPARSE CV
items.d: Name and one job only. Nothing should collapse or leave a huge void.

items.t: The same six with an EMPTY CV
items.d: No crash, no `undefined`, no `NaN`.

items.t: Accent colour is honoured in every one you check
items.d: Some templates ignore it, which reads as the setting being broken.

items.t: Premium templates are locked on free and open on Pro
items.d: And the lock is enforced server-side when rendering the PDF, not just in the picker.

items.t: Every preview image in the gallery loads
items.d: 61 cards. A missing preview is a template nobody will choose.

items.t: Download from the editor and from the dashboard
items.d: Both entry points.

items.t: The PDF matches the on-screen preview
items.d: Same fonts, same spacing, same page breaks. Open it in a real PDF reader, not the browser's inline viewer.
Four shapes that break differently.

items.t: Free plan: branding present. Pro: absent.
items.d: And confirm the Pro version really has none, on the last page too.

items.t: The free download limit is enforced
items.d: Five downloads in a calendar month, then the sixth is refused — by the server. Call /api/cvs/[id]/pdf directly to be sure.

items.t: The filename is something a person would keep
items.d: Not `download.pdf` or a UUID.

items.t: A render token cannot be reused across users
items.d: Take the PDF request from one account and replay it against another account's CV id. It must be refused.

sections.name: Sharing and the public CV page
sections.note: This is the one place private user data is deliberately exposed. Get it wrong and it gets indexed.

items.t: Free plan cannot create a share link
items.d: Hidden in the UI and refused by the API.

items.t: Pro can create one, and /cv/[shareId] opens in incognito
items.d: Signed out, in a different browser.
View source and check the robots meta. Then check /robots.txt disallows /cv/.
Revoke, then reload the old URL. 404, not a cached copy.

items.t: A guessed share id returns nothing
items.d: Change a character. No data, no error detail that helps a guesser.

items.t: The public page shows only the CV
items.d: No email address, no account details, no dashboard chrome.

sections.name: Payment — PayPal
sections.note: The only path where a bug costs money or a customer. PayPal is the sole gateway; Paddle has been removed.

items.d: The card reads: Pro, $9, every 31 days, cancellable, and YOUR email address.
$69, one-time, no renewal.

items.t: The checkout card is fully translated — in all three languages
items.d: Heading, order summary, all six feature bullets, the button, and the small print under it. This is where an English feature list sat under a French heading.

items.t: The request body contains a plan id and NO amount
items.d: Network tab → the POST to /api/payments/paypal/create-order. If a price, amount or currency appears in that body, a customer can name their own price.
Continue → PayPal sandbox → approve → return → /payment/success → the plan is active in /dashboard/account.
→ /payment/cancel. Nothing charged, no plan granted, and the page says so plainly.

items.t: Close the tab immediately after approving
items.d: The webhook must still grant the plan. Check /dashboard/account a minute later. This is the case a customer will hit on a phone.

items.t: Pay twice in a row for Pro
items.d: The second purchase must not double-charge or corrupt the expiry. Idempotent fulfilment is claimed — verify it.
Told there is nothing to buy, with a way back — not shown a pay button.

items.t: A Pro owner CAN still upgrade to Lifetime
items.d: That purchase must remain available.
Refused cleanly.
"Missing reference" and a way forward. Not a crash, not a spinner forever.

items.t: A forced failure is reported ENTIRELY in the page's language
items.d: The important one. Break PayPal on a preview deploy (wrong secret), set the site to French, and try to pay. The heading AND the body AND the next step must all be French. The old code rendered our API's English `message` in preference to the translated string sitting beside it — and it only ever showed on failure.
Approve, then kill your connection before the return. The page should tell you the payment may have gone through and not to pay twice.

items.t: The admin ledger records the order
items.d: /admin/payments shows it with the right plan, amount and provider.

items.t: No PADDLE_ variables remain in Vercel
items.d: Nothing reads them now. A live API key sitting in a dashboard that no code uses is a credential nobody is watching.
Not "the link is hidden" — type the URL. Then call /api/admin/users/[uid] directly and confirm 403.
Counts and readiness indicators load.
Search, pagination, detail.

items.t: Granting and revoking a plan by hand
items.d: Grant Pro to a test account, confirm the account sees it, revoke it, confirm it is gone.
Promote a test account to admin and back. Confirm the change takes effect on their next request.
The ledger, and a single order's detail.
Usage figures across 61 templates.
Inventory.
Should now report PayPal configured, Firebase configured, and no Paddle anywhere.
Correct production host. /api/, /dashboard/, /admin/, /cv/ and /payment/ disallowed.
Every public URL in all three languages. No /dashboard, no /admin, no /cv/[shareId], and no `localhost` — that last one has no runtime symptom at all.
Spot-check six pages across all three languages.
The English page points at fr and de; each of those points back at the other two and at x-default.
Paste three URLs into a link-preview debugger and look at the rendered card.
Google Rich Results Test on /, /pricing, a template page and a blog post — in each language.

items.t: noindex is on exactly the right pages
items.d: Present on /payment/*, /cv/[shareId], /dashboard/*, /admin/*. ABSENT from every marketing page — a stray noindex on /pricing is silent and expensive.
Install the PWA on a phone and look at the icon.
A real 404 status, in all three languages, with a way back.

items.t: No secret is in the client bundle
items.d: View source on /pricing, then search the /_next/static/*.js chunks for `pdl_`, `sk_`, `-----BEGIN`, your admin email and your PayPal secret. The browser is the only honest place to check this.

items.t: Another user's CV is not readable by id
items.d: GET /api/cvs/[someone-elses-id] while signed in as a different user. 403 or 404 — never their data.

items.t: Another user's CV is not editable by id
items.d: PATCH and DELETE the same id.

items.t: A normal user cannot change a plan
items.d: POST to /api/admin/users/[uid]/plan. 403.
Hammer /api/contact and the create-order endpoint. You should get 429 with a Retry-After, and the message should be translated.

items.t: Firestore rules deny direct client reads of other users' data
items.d: Test from the Firebase console rules simulator, not only through the app.

items.t: The contact form cannot be used to send mail as someone else
items.d: Submit with a spoofed from-address and check what actually arrives.

items.t: Private CV data is not indexed
items.d: Search `site:createcvonline.com` for /cv/ and /dashboard URLs. Do this after the site has been live a while, not just today.

items.t: 375px wide: nav, pricing cards, template grid, checkout
items.d: Nothing overflows horizontally. No two-finger zoom needed to read a price.

items.t: The editor on a real phone
items.d: Three tabs, keyboard does not cover the field you are typing into, drag-to-reorder works with touch.
Anything you have to aim at on a phone is a bug.
Mobile profile. Watch LCP and CLS specifically — the template grid is the likely CLS offender.

items.t: The template grid does not shift as images load
items.d: Reload with a throttled connection and watch.

items.t: The site is usable with JavaScript slow, not just absent
items.d: Throttle to Slow 3G and load /pricing. Anything that renders the wrong branch until hydration will show here — that class of bug put "this link is missing its payment reference" in front of paying customers.

sections.name: Five-minute smoke test
sections.note: Run this after EVERY deploy. If all seven pass, nothing structural is broken.

items.t: / loads in English, French and German
items.d: Three URLs, three languages, no console errors.
The computed numbers are a canary for the whole registry.
Count the grid or read the heading.
One account, one password.

items.t: Create a CV, type a name, reload — it persisted
items.d: Proves auth, Firestore write and autosave in one action.

items.t: Download a PDF and open it
items.d: Proves the render pipeline and the quota check.

items.t: /payment/checkout?plan=pro shows the PayPal button and the right price
items.d: Do not complete it. Just confirm the gateway is offered and says $9.
